```{r split-data}
set.seed(602)

```

```{r task2-rf-weighted}
# TODO: train a random forest with classwt = c("0" = 1, "1" = 5)
# Predictors: age, plan_tier, income, num_claims, support_calls, auto_pay, customer_rating
set.seed(602)
rf_wt <- NULL  # randomForest(factor(churned) ~ ..., classwt = c("0"=1,"1"=5), ntree=200)

# TODO: print the OOB confusion matrix
print(rf_wt)
```

```{r task2-compare-recall}
# Compute recall at threshold 0.5 for the weighted model
prob_wt   <- predict(rf_wt, test, type = "prob")[, "1"]
pred_wt   <- factor(ifelse(prob_wt > 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1))
cm_wt     <- table(Predicted = pred_wt, Actual = factor(test$churned))
recall_wt <- cm_wt["1", "1"] / sum(cm_wt[, "1"])

cat("Weighted RF recall at 0.5 threshold:", round(recall_wt, 3), "\n")
# Compare to naive recall (0): even at 0.5, the weighted model should find more churners
```

```{r task4-f1-threshold}
# Helper to compute F1 at a given threshold
f1_at <- function(prob, truth, threshold) {
  pred <- factor(ifelse(prob > threshold, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1))
  cm   <- table(pred, truth)
  TP   <- cm["1", "1"]
  FP   <- cm["1", "0"]
  FN   <- cm["0", "1"]
  P    <- if ((TP + FP) == 0) 0 else TP / (TP + FP)
  R    <- if ((TP + FN) == 0) 0 else TP / (TP + FN)
  if ((P + R) == 0) 0 else 2 * P * R / (P + R)
}
```

```{r task4-pr-curve}
# TODO: plot precision-recall curves for both models
# Use pROC or PRROC::pr.curve(), or manually compute precision and recall
# at a sequence of thresholds
thresholds <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.05)

# For rf_wt:
pr_df <- map_dfr(thresholds, function(thr) {
  pred <- factor(ifelse(prob_wt > thr, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1))
  cm   <- table(pred, factor(test$churned))
  TP   <- cm["1","1"]; FP <- cm["1","0"]; FN <- cm["0","1"]
  P    <- if ((TP+FP)==0) 0 else TP/(TP+FP)
  R    <- if ((TP+FN)==0) 0 else TP/(TP+FN)
  tibble(threshold = thr, precision = P, recall = R, model = "Weighted RF")
})

ggplot(pr_df, aes(x = recall, y = precision, colour = model)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Precision-Recall Curve", x = "Recall", y = "Precision") +
  theme_minimal()

# Which model gives a better trade-off? At what threshold?
```
